proofs.full_local_argument: This is a Curator reconstruction, separate from source text; no independent Reviewer check is claimed. Write S=sum_i L_i^alpha, ||.||=||.||_{1-alpha}, dual ||.||_*, and R=R_{1-alpha}(x0). Integrating coordinate Lipschitz continuity along x+uU_i h for 0<=u<=1 gives f(x+U_i h)<=f(x)+<g_i(x),h>+L_i||h||_2^2/2. Choosing h=-g_i(x)/L_i gives f(x)-f(T_i x)>=||g_i(x)||_2^2/(2L_i), so each step is nonincreasing. Fix y and define q(z)=f(z)-f(y)-<grad f(y),z-y>. Convexity gives q>=0 and q(y)=0; q has the same coordinate constants. Coordinate descent applied to q implies q(z)>=max_i ||U_i^T(grad f(z)-grad f(y))||_2^2/(2L_i). A maximum dominates its average under p_i, hence q(z)>=||grad f(z)-grad f(y)||_*^2/(2S). Add this inequality to the one with z,y interchanged to obtain ||grad f(z)-grad f(y)||_*^2/S <= <grad f(z)-grad f(y),z-y> <= ||grad f(z)-grad f(y)||_* ||z-y||. Division when nonzero proves weighted gradient Lipschitz continuity with constant S; the zero case is immediate. Integration on a full line segment therefore gives f(x)<=f(y)+<grad f(y),x-y>+S||x-y||^2/2. At y=x* in X*, grad f(x*)=0, so delta_0=f(x0)-f*<=SR^2/2=C/4 with C=2SR^2. Monotonicity keeps every realized x_t in the initial level set. Convexity and weighted duality give delta_t=f(x_t)-f*<=<grad f(x_t),x_t-x*><=R||grad f(x_t)||_* for any x* in X*. Conditional expected descent is at least sum_i p_i||g_i(x_t)||_2^2/(2L_i)=||grad f(x_t)||_*^2/(2S)>=delta_t^2/C when R>0. Let a_t=E delta_t. Jensen gives a_t-a_{t+1}>=a_t^2/C, while monotonicity gives 0<=a_{t+1}<=a_t. If a_0,...,a_k are positive, then 1/a_{t+1}-1/a_t=(a_t-a_{t+1})/(a_t a_{t+1})>=1/C, so 1/a_k>=1/a_0+k/C>=(k+4)/C. If some a_t=0, nonnegative gaps and monotonicity imply every later gap has expectation zero and the bound holds. If R=0, x0 equals a minimizer, all exact gradients vanish, and every iterate has zero gap. Thus a_k<=2SR^2/(k+4) in all cases. Finally <s,h>-||h||_2^2/2=||s||_2^2/2-||h-s||_2^2/2 proves that the Euclidean sharp map is s itself, verifying the specialization of the source update.

assumptions: f:R^N->R is convex and differentiable everywhere.
X* is nonempty and bounded, as assumed in source §2.
For every i=1,...,n, x in R^N and h in R^{n_i}, ||g_i(x+U_i h)-g_i(x)||_2<=L_i||h||_2, where L_i are known positive finite constants.
x0 is deterministic, alpha is fixed, and R_{1-alpha}(x0)<infinity.
Selected block gradients are exact. Given the full past, each draw has probability p_i; fresh independent draws realize this rule.
statement.conclusion: E[f(x_k)-f*] <= 2 S_alpha R_{1-alpha}(x0)^2/(k+4). This is a last-iterate expectation bound. Alpha=0 gives 2n R_1(x0)^2/(k+4). Alpha=1 gives 2(sum_i L_i)R_0(x0)^2/(k+4), where R_0 is the maximum Euclidean level-set radius.
statement.objects_and_definitions: R^N has n coordinate blocks R^{n_i}, N=sum_i n_i and I_N=(U_1,...,U_n). All block norms are Euclidean, g_i(x)=U_i^T grad f(x), X*=argmin f and f*=min f. S_alpha=sum_i L_i^alpha. For beta in R, ||v||_beta^2=sum_i L_i^beta||v^(i)||_2^2 and ||g||_{beta,*}^2=sum_i L_i^(-beta)||g^(i)||_2^2. R_beta(x0)=max_{f(x)<=f(x0)} max_{x* in X*}||x-x*||_beta. Iterates satisfy x_{t+1}=x_t-U_i_t g_i_t(x_t)/L_i_t with p_i=L_i^alpha/S_alpha.
statement.parameter_domains: n and n_i are positive integers; N=sum_i n_i; L_i in (0,infinity); alpha in R; k a nonnegative integer. Sampling and Lemma 2 explicitly allow real alpha although the source's intervening S_alpha notation paragraph says alpha>=0.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every finite block partition, every f, positive L_i, deterministic x0 and fixed alpha satisfying these conditions, and every integer k>=0, the conclusion holds with expectation over i_0,...,i_{k-1}. For k=0 there is no randomness.
